about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Nothing new on supply overnight; with Dec first notice next week the old-crop Dec/Mar spread and certificate flow matter more than headlines. Dec is sitting right on its 77.05 support, and high-grade certs remain a delivery risk for Dec longs rather than a comfort.
events: Dec ~77.06 (-0.26) on the 77.05 support; Mar ~81.05 (ICE via TradingView)
Crude falls again after API stock builds, a soft lead for synthetics (OilPrice.com)
Real still weak after Lula fiscal worries (Bloomberg)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil first: no new Centre-South crush data, but crude's renewed slide trims ethanol parity support for mills while the weak real keeps hedging sugar attractive. Mar has slipped back under the 18.02/17.92 supports overnight.
events: Mar ~17.91 (-0.26), low 17.75, below 17.92 support (ICE via TradingView)
API crude and gasoline builds pull oil lower, eroding Brazil ethanol parity (OilPrice.com)
BRL pressure from Lula fiscal worries keeps producer selling attractive (Bloomberg)

coffee.fundamental: ICE certified arabica stocks at a 1999 low and the widening Dec/Mar inverse still say deliverable coffee is scarce; the overnight dip back under 283.50 looks like profit-taking, not new supply. Antwerp/European stock levels and Brazil deliverability remain the things to watch.
events: ICE certified arabica stocks hit the lowest since 1999 (ADMIS, Barchart)
Dec ~282.15 (-4.45), back below 283.50 support; Mar ~277.85 (ICE via TradingView)
Nestle Brazil supplier labour hearing keeps forced-labour import-ban risk in view (Reuters, Daily Coffee News)

cocoa.fundamental: Rising ICE certified stocks keep the near-term balance looking comfortable; slow Ivory Coast port arrivals after heavy rains and dry-season mid-crop questions are the offsetting risks. No new ICCO quarterly bulletin yet (due end-November).
events: Ghana plans a raw-bean export ban by 2030 (Reuters)
